desc: Build a segment tree over original indices (1..N) that stores for each node: sum_P (sum of A_i * C_i), sum_S (sum of S_i), min_A, max_A, sum_A, count, lazy_P (number of times to add A_i to P_i), lazy_S (total B_Y to add to S_i). Initialize all to 0 except min_A, max_A, sum_A, count from A.

Implement the segment tree operations: apply(i, p, s) to apply lazy values to a node; push(i) to push lazy values to children; update(i, l, r, ql, qr, B) to apply update for threshold B; query(i, l, r, ql, qr) to get sum_P and sum_S for a range.

In the update function, if max_A[i] < B, return. If min_A[i] >= B and ql <= l and r <= qr, apply(i, 1, B) and return. Otherwise, push(i) and recurse to children. After recursion, update sum_P[i] and sum_S[i] from children.
In the query function, if ql <= l and r <= qr, return (sum_P[i], sum_S[i]). Otherwise, push(i) and combine results from children.
Read all queries, store them with their original index. Sort queries by Y in increasing order.
Precompute prefix sums of A and B.

Process queries: for each Y from 1 to N, call update(1, 0, size, 0, N, B[Y-1]) to add B_Y. Then for all queries with that Y, call query(1, 0, size, 0, X) to get sum_P and sum_S, and compute the answer using the formula.
Store answers in order of original index, then print them.
Ensure to use fast I/O and correct indexing (0-based or 1-based). Use size as power of 2 >= N.
